title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Podgora, Croatia 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Podgora? Adults-only TUI BLUE hotels, family options in nearby Tučepi, prices per night vs half-board and apartments.
content:
## Is There All-Inclusive in Podgora?

Not in the form most families look for. The town of Podgora itself has no large all-inclusive family resort. Its main hotel offer is half-board and bed-and-breakfast at the seafront Medora Auri Family Beach Resort (4★, several pools, spa, playground), plus a large stock of private apartments and villas. Tour operators sometimes bundle extra board options, so confirm the board type at booking.

All-inclusive does exist within the wider Podgora municipality, but only for adults. TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach, in Živogošće-Porat, is sold as adults-only all-inclusive. TUI BLUE Makarska, in Igrane, is a 4★ adults-only beach hotel with 179 rooms, two restaurants and a spa.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Hotels for Families

Families need to move a few kilometres away from Podgora:

- **Tučepi (about 4–5 km north):** Bluesun Hotel Neptun is the best-known family all-inclusive on this stretch. Its package covers three main meals, two snack meals, drinks, free bike rental and entertainment for all ages.
- **Podaca (about 25 km south):** Hotel Morenia sells all-inclusive, directly on the beach, with child-free offers.
- **Drvenik (about 35 km south):** Hotel Quercus, 100 m from the beach, sells all-inclusive.

Tučepi is the practical choice. It is a short drive, taxi or bus ride from Podgora, so a stay there still gives access to Podgora's beaches and restaurants.

## What All-Inclusive Typically Includes Here

- Breakfast (often with a late continental option), lunch and dinner as buffet
- One or two afternoon snacks
- House wine, beer, soft drinks and water with meals, and usually between meals at the bar
- Pool and beach access, sun loungers at many hotels
- Kids' and evening entertainment at family hotels

Usually excluded: premium spirits, bottled imported drinks, spa treatments, sun loungers on public beaches, excursions and parking. Croatian all-inclusive is often "light" compared with Turkey or Spain, with drink hours limited. Check the hours and brands before booking.

## Price Per Person Per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

Figures are rough, per adult sharing a double room, and move with the hotel category and booking date.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, late Sept–Oct) | Peak (mid-July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive hotel (4★) | €55–75 | €100–150 |
| Half-board hotel (3–4★) | €45–65 | €80–120 |
| Private apartment (room only) | €15–25 | €30–45 |
| Apartment plus food (self-catering and restaurants) | €40–55 | €55–75 |

Shoulder all-inclusive packages in Tučepi and Podaca run about €212–224 per person for 3–4 nights in autumn, roughly €55–70 a night. Peak-week packages in Živogošće start near €1,000 per person for 8 days, or about €125 a night. Half-board in Podgora and nearby autumn offers is about €63 a night per person. Children usually get large discounts or free places, which changes the maths for families.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in This Area

### Families with small children
All-inclusive works well for children under about 8. Meals are on schedule, snacks are available between meals, and there is no restaurant waiting at 19:30 with a tired toddler. Free or discounted child places make it competitive. Choose a resort with a pool and shallow entry, since Podgora's beaches are pebble.

### Short stays (2–5 nights)
Short stays favour hotels. There is no shopping, cooking or cleaning, and shoulder-season packages stay under €75 per night. Apartments often impose 5–7 night minimums in July and August.

### Couples without children
The adults-only TUI BLUE hotels suit couples who want quiet, a spa and a beachfront.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

Groups of friends, families with teenagers and anyone staying 7 nights or more usually do better in a Podgora apartment. Podgora has a supermarket within walking distance of most areas, a daily market and many konobas serving a grilled-fish dinner for €15–25 per head. Eating out once a day and cooking the rest typically costs less than all-inclusive in peak weeks.

Most travelers overestimate the value of all-inclusive in Podgora. The town's strength is its restaurant promenade and harbour, which all-inclusive guests rarely use. A resort in Tučepi or Živogošće makes sense only if you plan to stay at the hotel most of the day.

## Insider Tips

- Book peak-season all-inclusive by March; the cheapest family rooms sell out first.
- Compare the price per person with a child discount against an apartment for the whole family; a family of four often saves 30–40% in an apartment in August.
- Ask if drinks are included between meals and until what hour.
- For the best value, travel in late May, June or September, when the sea is warm and prices drop by about 40% from August.
- Without a car, check the distance to the beach and the bus connection; Podgora to Makarska is about 9 km.

## Quick Decision Guide

- Small children, 3–5 nights, shoulder season: all-inclusive in Tučepi.
- Couple wanting quiet: adults-only TUI BLUE in Živogošće or Igrane.
- Family of four for 7+ nights in August: apartment in Podgora.
- Flexible half-board with sea access in town: Medora Auri Family Beach Resort.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Podgora?
faq.answer: Not a family all-inclusive in the town centre; Podgora hotels mostly sell half-board or breakfast. Adults-only all-inclusive exists at TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće and TUI BLUE Makarska in Igrane, both in Podgora municipality.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive for families near Podgora?
faq.answer: Tučepi, about 4–5 km north, has Bluesun Hotel Neptun, which offers all-inclusive with meals, snacks, drinks and entertainment. Further south, Podaca (Hotel Morenia) and Drvenik (Hotel Quercus) also sell it.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person per night near Podgora?
faq.answer: About €55–75 in shoulder season and €100–150 in peak season (July–August), depending on the hotel. Half-board is typically €45–65 shoulder and €80–120 peak.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than an apartment in Podgora?
faq.answer: No, usually not. An apartment with groceries and one restaurant meal a day costs about €40–55 per person in shoulder season and €55–75 in peak, below the all-inclusive range.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive worth it for families with small children?
faq.answer: Yes, for short stays with children under about 8, particularly when child places are free or discounted. For stays of a week or more with older children, a self-catering apartment is usually cheaper.

quickAnswer: Podgora has almost no true all-inclusive family hotels. The adults-only TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach (Živogošće) and TUI BLUE Makarska (Igrane), both in Podgora municipality, sell all-inclusive. Families find it in nearby Tučepi (Bluesun Hotel Neptun). Expect about €55–75 per person per night in shoulder season and €100–150 in peak.
